title: "Traveler's Diarrhea and Its Treatment During Military Deployments of Bundeswehr Personnel Operating Remotely"
summary: Traveler's diarrhea still affects one in four travelers, particularly during short trips (<30 days) to tropical and subtropical regions. The U.S. Armed Forces have reported a significant impact on operational readiness due to traveler’s diarrhea in conflicts over recent decades, partly because hygienic prophylaxis cannot always be maintained in military contexts. A watch-and-wait approach with fluid and electrolyte replacement may not be feasible for tactical reasons. Since 2018, Bundeswehr units frequently deployed on short-term missions have been equipped with the option to include an antibiotic alongside an anti-motility agent in their personal travel medical kits, following proper briefing and the provision of a pocket guide. To date, no data exist on traveler’s diarrhea and its impact on German military personnel.
